steps: Touch your dominant thumb to your fingertips to make a flattened O handshape.
Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you, palm facing up.
Set the flattened O onto the open palm, then slide it forward and off the hand.
Keep the moving hand's palm angled down as it brushes along and leaves the base palm.
Face the direction of the seller, since the forward motion shows money changing hands.
tip: “Buying” is signed with the base BUY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Shape both hands into flat open hands with fingertips together, like the starting position of the PLEASE sign.
Place your right flat hand on your upper chest and your left flat hand on your belly, an inch or two out from your body.
Circle both hands at the same time in opposite directions, with the right hand looping clockwise and the left hand counterclockwise.
Angle your palms inward toward your torso so the fingertips of each hand point toward the other hand.
Wear a warm, content smile while signing, since the sign conveys pleasure and delight.
tip: Past form of “Enjoy” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat in front of you with the palm facing up.
Touch the tip of your dominant index finger to the center of the open palm.
Flick the index finger forward off the palm toward the person being paid.
Keep the moving finger's palm facing sideways during the flick.
Aim the flick at the recipient and keep your expression matter-of-fact.
tip: “Paying” is signed with the base PAY sign — ASL/BSL marks ongoing action on the sign, not with a separate word.

steps: Make Y handshapes with both hands, thumbs and pinkies extended.
Hold both Y-hands in front of your chest, a few inches apart.
Twist both wrists back and forth in a playful alternating shake.
Keep the palms facing toward each other through the whole shake.
Smile and look lively, since PLAY always carries a fun feeling.
tip: Past form of “Play” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.

steps: Form a Y-handshape with your dominant hand by stretching your thumb and pinkie wide while folding the middle fingers down.
Raise the hand to chest height in front of you with the palm facing down.
Press the hand firmly downward in one short, decisive stroke, as if pinning something in place.
Hold the Y-handshape rigid the whole time, keeping the thumb and pinkie fully extended.
Repeat the downward press with both hands together when you want extra emphasis.
Keep a firm, settled expression — this is a command to hold position, not a question.
tip: Past form of “Stay” — signed with the base sign; time is shown separately, not on the verb.
